description:
SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY
Superior-Union
SHERIFF'S SALE NO. 26002074
DOCKET NO. F00277826
PLAINTIFF – PROVIDENT BANK, SUCCESSOR BY MERGER TO LAKELAND BANK
DEFENDANTS- AROLDO R. CALDERON
Writ of Execution.
By virtue of the above stated Writ of Execution to me directed and delivered I will expose for sale at public venue on
Wednesday THE 21st DAY OF October 2026
between the hours of two and five o'clock in the afternoon of said day, that is to say at 2:00 P.M. prevailing time at Warinanco Ice Skating Center, 1 Park Drive, Roselle, New Jersey 07203 to wit:
All that tract or parcel of land, situate, lying and being in the town of ELIZABETH, County of Union and State of New Jersey:
Being known as: BLOCK 444 LOT 10
PREMISES COMMONLY KNOWN AS:
848-850 GIBBONS COURT A/K/A 844 GIBBONS COURT ELIZABETH, NJ 07202
A more complete metes and bounds description can be found in the Office of the Union County Sheriff.
Lien(s)/Taxes: Dimensions (approx.): 33.33 ftx 150.12 32.81 ftx 00.62 ft x 152.24 ft
As the above description does not constitute a full legal description, said full legal description is contained in the Owners' Deed which is recorded in the Union County Clerk's Office in Deed Book 6500, Page 2303 et seq. and which is referenced in that certain mortgage recorded in the Union County Clerk's Office in M01tgage-2 Book 15335, Page 2153 et seq., City
of Elizabeth, New Jersey and the Writ of Execution on file with the Sheriff of Union County.
Amount Due for Taxes: As of September 8, 2026, the taxes due and owing is in the amount of $2,240.86
Amount Due for Water
Assessments: As of September 8, 2026, water assessments are due and owing in the amount of $ 1 15.33
The occupancy status of the property is unknown.
The outstanding taxes and water assessments due and owing will be updated at the time of sale. Buyers must also check with the City of Elizabeth Tax Collector and Liberty Water Company.
Good faith estimated of upset price: $408,169.37
Surplus Money: If after the sale and satisfaction of the mortgage debt, including costs and expenses, there remains any surplus money, the money will be deposited into the Superior Court Trust Fund and any person claiming the surplus, or any part thereof, may file a motion pursuant to
Court Rules, 4:64-3 and 4:57-2 stating the nature and extent of that person's claim and asking for
Page 1 of 2
https://seidmanllc.sharepoint.com/sites/seidmanteam/Shared Documents/General/Provident Bank v. Calderon/Sheriffs Sale Package/Short Form Description of Property.docx
an order directing payment of the surplus money. The Sheriff or other person conducting the sale will have information regarding the surplus, if any.
THE SHERIFF RESERVES THE RIGHT TO ADJOURN THIS SALE WITHOUT
FURTHER NOTICE THROUGH PUBLICATION
Note: The street address is merely given as a convenience to the bidders and is not a representation of fact on the part of the sheriff. The diagram or concise description does not constitute a full legal description of the premises, but it can be found in the Union County Sheriff Office.
Subject to any unpaid taxes, municipal liens or other charges, and any such taxes, charges, liens, insurance premiums or other advances made by plaintiff prior to this sale. All interested parties are to conduct and rely upon their own independent investigation to ascertain whether or not any outstanding interest remain of record and/or have priority over the lien being foreclosed and, if so the current amount due thereon.
If the sale is set aside for any reason, the Purchaser at the sale shall be entitled only to a return of the deposit paid. The Purchaser shall have no further recourse against the Mortgagor, the Mortgagee and the Mortgagee’s attorney.
Surplus Money: If after the sale and satisfaction of the mortgage debt, including costs and expenses, there remains any surplus money, the money will be deposited into the Superior Court Trust Fund and any person claiming the surplus, or any part thereof, may file a motion pursuant to Court Rules 4:64-3 and 4:57-2 stating the nature and extent of that person's claim and asking for an order directing payment of the surplus money. The Sheriff or other person conducting the sale will have information regarding the surplus, if any.
The approximate amount due on this execution is $404,019.47 plus interest, cost, printers’ fees, Sheriff's fees and commission. The prior liens, as per affidavit of consideration are not a representation of fact on the part of the Sheriff.
Peter D. Corvelli
SHERIFF
